title: Estado Novo
capsule: The Estado Novo ('New State') was the authoritarian corporatist regime that governed Portugal from Lisbon, formally established by the constitution approved in the referendum of 19 March 1933 and consolidated under António de Oliveira Salazar, prime minister from 1932 until a disabling stroke in 1968. It grew out of the military dictatorship installed by the coup of 28 May 1926 that ended the First Republic, and it suppressed opposition through the secret police (PVDE, later PIDE) while keeping Portugal officially neutral in World War II. The regime clung to a colonial empire across Africa and Asia and waged the Portuguese Colonial War from 1961; under Salazar's successor Marcelo Caetano it proved unable to end that conflict, and the Armed Forces Movement's Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974 brought it down. The dataset envelope (1926 onward) reflects the regime's origins in the 1926 coup and the continuity of the Portuguese state thereafter, not the persistence of the Estado Novo itself, which ended in 1974.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Metropolitan Portugal's boundaries are precisely documented; the colonial territories grouped under this entry varied substantially over the period and their geometric representation as a single polity is an editorial simplification. The to-year of 2024 is a dataset artifact.
